findings.title: An existing output link can be replaced
findings.description: `main` uses `existsSync(out)` to decide whether the destination is free, then renames the staging directory over that path. A dangling symlink passes the check and is replaced on Unix; another process can likewise create a regular file between the check and rename, contrary to the builder’s promise not to replace an entry it did not make.

citations.citation:
* Usage: `git log --format='%H%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%B%x1e' | node scripts/build-site.ts
 * --commit <sha> --repo-url <url> --out <dir>`. Makes `<dir>` (it must not exist; its parent
 * must) and writes `notes.json`, `notes.md`, `build.json`
 * and `index.html` into `<dir>`.
 * Exit codes: 0 the files are written, 1 the input was refused and nothing was written, 2 usage.

evidence.explanation: The destination is checked once before four staged writes, and `renameSync` later uses it without another ownership check. A dangling symlink is an existing directory entry even though `existsSync` reports its missing target as absent; on Unix, renaming a directory over a symlink or regular file replaces that entry, not its target.

findings.title: Restrictive file modes block publishing
findings.description: `main` changes the staging directory to mode `0755` but leaves the four files at the modes assigned by `writeFileSync` under the process umask. With a restrictive Unix umask such as `077`, the files remain `0600`, the new permissions test fails, and a Pages artifact built under that configuration can be refused.

citations.citation: Pages maintainers describe deployment permissions errors for unreadable artifacts and note that the upload action no longer fixes those permissions.

evidence.explanation: The build chmods only `staging`, whereas the test requires each generated file to be `0644`. GitHub’s Pages deployment maintainers confirm that artifacts with unreadable files can produce a deployment permissions error and that the upload action does not repair permissions for the workflow.

findings.title: Windows log streams cannot build a site
findings.description: `buildSite` accepts only an empty tail or `\n` after the final record separator, while `parseGitLog` also accepts `\r\n` framing. When a Windows shell re-encodes a Git log pipe with CRLF endings, parsing would succeed but the site build rejects the stream before writing files.

evidence.explanation: `parseGitLog` explicitly removes CRLF framing when a Windows shell re-encodes the pipe, but the added tail check excludes `\r\n`.

findings.title: Day 20 journal describes an older build script
findings.description: The 'What was built' section of `journal/day-20.md` says the script refuses 'an output directory that is not empty' and has '13 tests'. The final script refuses any output path that already exists, empty or not, and the suite has 19 tests, as line 61 of the same journal says, so anyone reading this section will get the contract wrong.

citations.citation:
- `scripts/build-site.ts`: from a git log stream, a commit and a repository URL, the four files
  Pages serves: `notes.json` and `notes.md` (byte-identical to `tracenotes render`),
  `build.json` (the commit and the number of commits, no time) and a fixed `index.html`. It
  refuses a history with no commit, with a malformed record, or that does not start at the
  commit being published; input that is not valid UTF-8; a repository URL `render` rejects; an
  output directory that is not empty.
- `tests/build-site.test.ts`: 13 tests, red before the script existed
  (`evidence/day20/t041/tests-red.txt`).
- `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: on a push to `main` only. The build job reads the repository
  (full history, no stored credential), refuses a shallow clone and runs the script; the deploy
  job holds the two Pages permissions and runs nothing from the repository.
- `README.md`, `FACTORY.md` (publish step, monitors, gate row, one known gap), `BACKLOG.md`.

Checks after the review rounds below: `npm run check` on Windows, 415 tests, 414 pass, 1 skipped
(396 before; the skipped one checks file modes, which Windows does not have). The build-site
tests on Linux, in a `node:24-slim` container: 19 of 19. By hand on `main` at `ebb67dd`: the
build exits 0 with 122 commits, and `cmp` finds `notes.json` and `notes.md` identical to the
output of `node src/cli.ts render`.

evidence.explanation: The final `main` refuses any path that exists (`existsSync(out)`, message 'already exists'). The journal's own checks paragraph counts 19 build-site tests, but the 'What was built' list still describes the review-1 design.

+  commit being published; input that is not valid UTF-8; a repository URL `render` rejects; an
+  output directory that is not empty.
+- `tests/build-site.test.ts`: 13 tests, red before the script existed
+  (`evidence/day20/t041/tests-red.txt`).
